tbprogress: Tracking country progress towards the WHO End TB milestones

Documentation website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-avat0006-ai/

Purpose

tbprogress is an R package that bundles World Health Organization (WHO) estimates of tuberculosis (TB) incidence and mortality for 215 countries and territories, 2000-2023, a few functions for analysing them, and a Shiny app for exploring them.

The app is designed for a public-health analyst or policy student who wants to answer one question:

Is a country’s TB burden falling fast enough to meet the WHO End TB milestones, and how does it compare with its region?

The WHO End TB Strategy asks countries to cut the TB incidence rate and the number of TB deaths by set percentages compared with 2015 (for example, a 50% cut in the incidence rate and a 75% cut in deaths by 2025). The app lets you pick up to five countries, see their trajectories against the milestone path, and check whether each is on track, behind or rising.

Installation

Install the package from GitHub (you need the remotes package, available from CRAN):

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-avat0006-ai")

The package needs R 4.1 or newer. Its dependencies (shiny, bslib, DT, dplyr, ggplot2, rlang, tibble) are installed automatically.

Launch the app 

library(tbprogress)
run_tb_app()

The app opens in your browser. It uses only the data inside the installed package, so it needs no internet connection and no extra files. It has three tabs:

  • Progress: a headline count of countries on track, a trajectory chart for each selected country against the WHO milestone path, and a status table.
  • Peers: where each country sits among all countries in its WHO region.
  • Guide: what each control does, how to read each output, and the caveats.

See the Getting started vignette for a guided walk-through.

Using the functions without the app 

library(tbprogress)

# Which countries are on track for the WHO deaths milestone in 2023?
s <- tb_progress_summary(indicator = "mortality", assess_year = 2023)
table(s$status)

# Plot three countries against the milestone path
plot_tb_trajectory(indicator = "incidence",
                   countries = c("Kenya", "India", "Brazil"))
Function What it does
run_tb_app() Launches the Shiny app.
tb_progress_summary() Per-country reduction since 2015 versus the reduction WHO requires, with a status.
tb_index() Rescales a country’s burden so 2015 = 100.
tb_required_reduction() The reduction the WHO milestone path requires in any year.
plot_tb_trajectory(), plot_tb_peers() The two charts used in the app.
tb_status_table(), tb_app_theme() The table and theme used in the app.

The data

Two datasets are included (see ?tb_burden and ?tb_targets for every variable):

  • tb_burden: 5,117 rows (one per country-year) and 18 variables, including incidence_rate (new cases per 100,000 people), mortality_n (estimated TB deaths), population and who_region.
  • tb_targets: the WHO End TB milestones (percentage reductions required compared with 2015).

Source, licence and attribution

  • Source: World Health Organization (WHO), global tuberculosis programme data (https://www.who.int/teams/global-tuberculosis-programme/data). The same WHO estimates are published on the WHO data portal. The CSV used here was obtained from the TidyTuesday 2025-11-11 release, curated by Darakhshan Nehal from the getTBinR package by Sam Abbott.
  • Milestones: WHO (2015), The End TB Strategy, Geneva: World Health Organization.
  • Data licence: WHO publishes its data on data.who.int under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0) with additional WHO terms. This package complies with those terms:
    • WHO is credited as the source (citation below).
    • The meaning of the data is not altered. Changes made: columns were renamed, a subset of variables was kept, and who_region was made a factor. No data values were changed (see data-raw/tb_burden.R).
    • This package, its app and its analyses are not endorsed by or affiliated with WHO. The WHO name and emblem are not used as branding.
    • WHO’s separate data policy also limits use to public-health, non-commercial purposes, so the data are used here for educational purposes only.
  • Suggested citation: World Health Organization 2026 data.who.int, Tuberculosis incidence (per 100 000 population) [Indicator]. https://data.who.int/indicators/i/13B4226/C288D13 (Accessed on 31 October 2026, via the TidyTuesday copy described above).
  • Package licence: the code is released under the MIT licence (see LICENSE). That licence does not extend to the WHO data.

These are modelled estimates. The WHO uncertainty intervals are not part of the dataset used here, so small differences should be interpreted with caution.

Reproducing the data

The scripts in data-raw/ rebuild the package data from the raw CSV (data-raw/who_tb_data.csv), downloading it first if it is missing:

source("data-raw/tb_burden.R")   # builds data/tb_burden.rda
source("data-raw/tb_targets.R")  # builds data/tb_targets.rda
